subject: Post-call: Benchmark protocol & dataset format for model-fit evaluation
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Emily Ross <emily.ross@mediassist.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Benchmark protocol & dataset format for model-fit evaluation

Hi Emily — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Summary of discovery
- Primary goal: reduce triage time for care coordinators by surfacing correct patient intent and recommended next action from intake notes.
- Accuracy target: net gain vs. current rules baseline (F1) >= 12 pts; hallucination rate < 3% on the test set.
- Latency: 95th pct token latency target <= 150ms for 512 tokens in dedicated mode.

Redwood recommended candidate models to trial
- instruction-tuned-13B (quantized 4-bit) — good balance of accuracy and cost for long-form structured outputs
- instruct-7B-v2 — fast baseline for throughput-sensitive routes
- fallback: smaller condensed policy model for short responses to keep costs predictable

Files & links I dropped in the shared folder (Drive link below)
- scoring_template.xlsx (attached) — suggested rubric (exact match, normalized string score, semantic-similarity thresholds)
- prompt_set_v1.csv (attached) — representative prompt templates and expected output examples
- quick benchmark runner link — shared in related_links for your engineering team

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Can you share a 200–500 item sample (anonymized) in JSONL format. See format guidance in the scoring_template (id, input, expected_output, category). If you prefer, we can accept a pseudo-anonymized CSV.
2) Confirm whether PHI will be in the dataset. If yes, we will send instructions for secure upload (S3 presigned link + optional VPC-only transfer).
3) We’ll run an initial 1k-item smoke benchmark using the two recommended models above and return a short deck with token-cost estimates and per-category failure modes.

Attachments: mediassist_sample_prompts.csv (csv), scoring_template.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks — I’ll loop Karthik in for the technical eval plan.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
https://redwood.com

Thanks Tessa — this is great and aligns with what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- We can provide a ~300-item sample. It will include PHI in the raw notes; we need instructions for de-identification and secure upload.
- Our priority categories are: "intake_intent", "insurance_issue", "care_coordination", "scheduling". We can label expected_output at a coarse level for the sample; full annotation will take more time.
- Are you able to run a hallucination audit (we call it a "groundedness check") as part of the smoke run? We want explicit false-positive examples flagged.

I attached a small sample extract (mediassist_sample_dataset.jsonl) — redacted but representative. Mike and I are available for a 30-min tech sync Friday morning if that helps.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emily Ross <emily.ross@mediassist.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2026 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Benchmark protocol & dataset format for model-fit evaluation

Emily — thanks for the sample. Below is the technical evaluation protocol we’ll execute for the smoke benchmark and the 1k-run if you approve. I’ve attached a more detailed markdown with commands (eval_instructions.md) and the prompt set we plan to use (prompt_set_v1.csv).

Dataset format (required for automated runner)
- Format: JSONL, UTF-8 encoded, newline-delimited.
- Required fields per line: id (string), input (string), expected_output (string, coarse label ok), category (string), source (string optional).
- Max sample size for initial smoke run: 1k records; file size < 50MB recommended.

Scoring & metrics
- Primary: micro and macro F1 on the coarse labels (intake_intent, insurance_issue, etc.).
- Secondary: normalized string similarity (BLEURT or sentence-transformer cosine) for structured generation outputs. Thresholds: similarity >= 0.78 considered acceptable.
- Hallucination / groundedness: we will run a binary check per output — does the model assert facts not present in input? Flag rate target: <3% for high-severity categories.
- Latency & cost: measure tokens-per-second and per-token inference cost using your expected traffic mix. We’ll provide cost estimates across our hosted and dedicated pricing.

Evaluation runner & data handling
- Upload options: secure S3 presigned link (preferred) or encrypted Drive share. If PHI is included, choose S3 presigned and we’ll trigger a VPC-only ingest process.
- Data retention: by default Redwood keeps datasets associated with eval jobs for 30 days; we can shorten retention for regulated workloads.

Deliverables for the smoke run (48–72 hours)
- CSV summary of per-category precision/recall/F1
- Top 20 failure examples with short notes on root cause (prompt issue, model hallucination, tokenization mismatch)
- Latency & cost table (hosted vs. dedicated)
- Recommended next steps: fine-tune vs. instruction-tune vs. retrieval-augmented approach

Attachments: eval_instructions.md (md), prompt_set_v1.csv (csv)

Please confirm: 1) sample upload method (S3 vs Drive), 2) whether you want the smoke run to include both recommended models, and 3) availability for the 30-min tech sync Friday 10:00–10:30am ET.

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
